newsitem.title: USA: Discovery Zone replaces chief executive.
newsitem.headline: Discovery Zone replaces chief executive.

text.p: Discovery Zone Inc, the insolvent commercial-playground group, appointed theme-parks executive Scott Bernstein as its chief executive, The Miami Herald newspaper said on Wednesday.
A spokesman for Discovery Zone was not immediately available.
But the Herald, quoting company sources, said Bernstein replaced Donna Moore, chief executive for 17 months, on December 5. No public announcement was made of the switch.
Bernstein, 36, had been president of northeastern operations of the Six Flags theme parks, partly owned by Time Warner Inc .

Moore, 57, will remain chairwoman of Discovery Zone, operator of 225 indoor play centers, until a banruptcy court approves the company's reorganization plan, the newspaper said. It has been shutting outlets and has some $350 million in debt.

The formerly high-flying Discover Zone, whose stock-market value totalled $1.3 billion three years ago, is now controlled by an investment group lead by Martin Davis, former chairman of Paramount Communications Inc.

Davis and other investors gained control of the company, whose shares were delisted by the Nasdaq Stock Market last spring, by buying up Discovery Zone's bank debt at a deep discount, the Herald said.
